title: Quiz 3 – Brute Force & Exhaustive Search (NP concepts)
notes: Brute-force (exhaustive) search systematically enumerates candidates and checks feasibility/optimality.
Week 3 - Brute Force and Exhaustive Search.pdf
Examples covered: Selection Sort, Bubble Sort, Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP), 0/1 Knapsack, DFS, BFS.
Week 3 - Brute Force and Exhaustive Search.pdf
Exhaustive search is often exponential in worst case due to exploring all permutations/subsets/paths.

NP: decision problems whose YES instances can be verified in polynomial time given a certificate.
Week 3 - Brute Force and Exhaustive Search.pdf
NP-hard: at least as hard as every problem in NP (no requirement to be in NP/decidable as decision).
Week 3 - Brute Force and Exhaustive Search.pdf
Week 3 - Brute Force and Exhaustive Search.pdf
Brute force solutions exist for NP-complete problems (e.g., TSP, Knapsack) but run in exponential time.
Week 3 - Brute Force and Exhaustive Search.pdf
DFS/BFS are exhaustive in the sense of exploring the search space; their runtime depends on branching factor and depth.
